 La Roche-Posay to Neutrogena: New BEMT sunscreens hitting shelves in the US
 By
 Lollie Hancock 
 | Published: 23-Oct-2026 
 Ingredients 
 Sun Care 
 Bemotrizinol (BEMT) is the first new ingredient approved by the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for use in over-the-counter SPFs in the states since 1999. Now, brands such as La Roche-Posay, Neutrogena and Ultra Violette have launched new skus in the US formulated with the BEMT

 Click here to find out more. 
 Earlier this year, the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) added bemotrizinol to its list of permitted sunscreen active ingredients for use in the states, the first update to approved actives for sun protection since 1999.
 Although Bemotrizinol, abbreviated as BEMT, has been used across the EU, Asia and other territories for many years, it is only in 2026 that over-the-counter sunscreens in the US can now be formulated with the ingredient, with products permitted to contain concentration levels of up to 6%.
 Now, beauty brands are racing to release sun care skus in the US formulated with the newly approved ingredients, with La Roche-Posay , Neutrogena and Ultra Violette among the first to get through the gate.
 Nutrition, health and beauty chemical company DSM-Firmenich was given exclusive rights to produce BEMT in the US under the name Parsol Shield.
 Unlike mineral SPF formulations, sunscreens made with BEMT apply clear to the skin, with minimal absorption making the formulas well suited to sensitive or acne-prone skin.
 The ingredient protects skin against both ageing and long-term damage from UVA rays, and surface sunburn from UVB.

 La Roche-Posay has launched its first Anthelios sunscreen comprising BEMT – Anthelios UV Defense SPF 50 Sunscreen.
